answer: One identity stakes 80 for a glacier pearl bed at one site, filing distances to three glacier landmarks, sealed by a cipher from distances, pearl serial, key. Auditors check the distances triangulate to an unclaimed site and the cipher matches; a duplicate site, inconsistent distances, or reused cipher forfeits the stake. First filing 37, rising 6 per filing, so the thousandth costs 6,031; a thousand fake beds cost 3,034,000 in fees plus 80,000 staked. Rented sites fail: same distances and cipher on a second key forfeit both stakes. A genuine diver pays 37 once, stake back at window close.
